 Summary
 Saints win 3-2 at West Ham through Matsuki after 100 seconds and Bree stunner before Walker-Peters brilliantly pulls one back but Dobbin adds third before Soucek gives Hammers late hope
 Swansea beaten 5-0 at QPR after Kone hat-trick inside 15 minutes and two for Dunne 
 Burnley went ahead at Lincoln but lose 4-1 thanks to House, Ladefoged, Jefferies and a Ladefoged second before Edwards has penalty saved for Clarets
 Wolves edge past Hornets through Armstrong goal
 Cardiff penalty saved before scoring only goal against Birmingham
 Blackburn win 2-0 against Wrexham thanks to Gudjohnsen double
 Hughes puts rock-bottom Preston ahead but West Brom snatch equaliser 
 Stoke v Bristol City ends goalless
 Earlier struggling Norwich win 3-1 at Charlton; Portsmouth 2-1 Millwall; Sheffield United earn 1-1 draw against 10-man Derby

 Show Most recent Most popular 'The signs are really good' published at 17:30 BST 17:30 BST 
 FT: Charlton 1-3 Norwich 
 Norwich City 
 Media caption, Norwich City head coach Philippe Clement reacts to the 3-1 victory at Charlton
 Norwich City head coach Philippe Clement told BBC Radio Norfolk: 
 "Everybody is united in this group, otherwise you cannot come back after going behind here. Those signs are really good.
 "The dressing room is really good, it's now (about) getting consistency in the performances and game management. 
 "I told them that they need to feel happy, this is just the start we needed to fuel their confidence for the weeks and months to come. They can still do better."

 'Toxic scenes as Burnley face their fans' published at 17:24 BST 17:24 BST 
 FT: Lincoln 4-1 Burnley 
 Andy Sixsmith 
Final Score reporter 
 Toxic scenes at full time in the Burnley end. 
 Credit to the players for going over to the fans - but the supporters break out into boos and chants of, ‘You’re not fit to wear the shirt’ at the team. 
 Banners unfurled against owners ALK and Alan Pace too - with the future of Nicky Hayen in serious jeopardy.

 'You have to acclimatise to where you are' published at 17:20 BST 17:20 BST 
 FT: West Ham 2-3 Southampton 
 Paul Parker 
Ex-QPR and Manchester United defender on BBC Radio London 
 I'm not going to say Southampton were better. Yes they won the game but they have knowhow about this league West Ham didn't have much about them.
 They need a centre-forward.
 West Ham are playing too much nicey, nicey stuff. A lot of the players need to understand this league. You have to acclimatise to where you are and a lot of these players don't want to do it and they can't get their head around where they are.

 get involved Get Involved published at 17:19 BST 17:19 BST 
 Click the yellow button at the top left of this page 
 As much as Burnley are clearly struggling, Lincoln deserve more credit. I actually tipped them to possibly reach the play-offs, and while that was probably a bit generous they look like they'll finish comfortably in mid-table.
 Tobias, Brighton 
 A journey of a thousand points begins with a single point against the Baggies.
Come on Preston let's put a run together and climb that table! Get to January and get some players in (and out, defensive rebuild needed) and let's have a real good go at staying up!
 Mark, Preston 
 Stoke still on the up. 
Clean sheet and another point. Top teams would have won that game against a Bristol side who had no intentions of trying to win the game. 
Keep building and next year hopefully we win the games. 
Up the Potters
 Chris, Stoke 
 Bit early to be thinking about next season, isn't it, Chris?

 Weakness in attack exposed for Birmingham published at 17:15 BST 17:15 BST 
 FT: Cardiff 1-0 Birmingham 
 Laura Kenyon 
BBC 5Live reporter at Cardiff City Stadium 
 It could have been far more but in the end, just a solitary goal seals all three points for Cardiff. 
 It is a game that has exposed possible shortcomings in Birmingham's attacking calibre. Never really looked like scoring.
 Yes, two big chances at the end of the game but took 90 minutes before posing a proper threat. 
 Demarai Gray with the biggest opportunity missed. A decision to go left or right of the keeper and Gray scores a huge late equaliser and keeps the pressure on the top two. He opted to go down the middle and summed up a frustrating game for the visitors.

 'Strong bond between Saints players and fans' published at 17:13 BST 17:13 BST 
 FT: West Ham 2-3 Southampton 
 Marc Webber 
BBC Final Score commentator at the London Stadium 
 The Southampton fans were reluctant to leave as they celebrate a win with their players.
 The players respond and celebrate with them.
 Their side faced a late battle and the sense of embattlement the club has been under of late has clearly led to a strong bond between the team and supporters.

 Wolves, Saints and R's make gains published at 17:11 BST 17:11 BST 
 Championship table 
 Image source, Getty Images It has been a great weekend for Middlesbrough, who climbed to the top of the Championship table with a thumping 5-1 over Bolton last night and end the weekend at the summit, courtesy of defeats for Swansea and West Ham.
 The Hammers were beaten by Southampton, who move up to sixth while Wolves climbed to fourth with victory over Watford.
 QPR's 5-0 battering of the Swans takes them back into the play-off places. 
 At the bottom, Burnley remain in the relegation zone after they were thrashed 4-1 by Lincoln, while Preston are now five points adrift of safety at the foot of the table after West Brom came from behind to draw at Deepdale.

 'Peretz save shows you need a keeper to win you points' published at 17:08 BST 17:08 BST 
 FT: West Ham 2-3 Southampton 
 Jo Tessem 
Ex-Southampton midfielder on BBC Radio Solent 
 I have to give the man of the match to Daniel Peretz because that unbelievable save at the end keeps them in the game.
 It was nervy in the way that the second half was quite open. We couldn't keep the ball as we did in the first half. When you're 3-1 you need to keep the ball and it made the game exciting.
 But that save at the end from Peretz shows you need a keeper to win you the points and that's the difference between getting the three points rather than two.
 A solid defensive display by Schlotterbeck and Stephens as well as Ward-Prowse.
 73 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Humiliation for Swansea at Loftus Road published at 17:06 BST 17:06 BST 
 FT QPR 5-0 Swansea 
 Mark Poyser 
BBC Radio Wales commentator at Loftus Road 
 Vitor Matos' men stand in front of the rain soaked away end holding up their hands in apology after a dreadful afternoon in west London.
 A goal down inside two minutes, 3-0 behind after a quarter of an hour courtesy of a remarkable Richard Kone hat-trick.
 Captain Jimmy Dunne then bagged a brace himself to inflict Swansea's worst league defeat in three years.
 Before today the Swans had conceded just eight goals this season, a total nearly doubled during a chaotic 90 minutes at Loftus Road.
 As bad as the visitors were, Rangers were tremendous and defied their injury problems to return to form.

 What a great league the Championship is. Stoke after 12 games: 9th, not bad. Also Stoke after 12 games: 3 pts off automatic spots, great start.

 As a QPR fan in the US, waking up early for this team has been occasionally more effort than it’s worth. Today that is not the case. Delighted and optimistic - this team has a bright future.

 Completely toxic atmosphere at Burnley now. Fans in revolt, clueless board, out-of-depth manager and players completely disinterested. Horror show and we're still some time off Halloween. Need more than a sacked manager to fix this mess.

BBC WM commentator 
 Wolves dominated the first half but they were never so fluent in the second.
 Adam Armstrong took his goal well and they'll be glad he did as they squeeze in the win.

 FULL-TIME published at 16:56 BST 16:56 BST 
 Wolves 1-0 Watford 
 A better second half from Watford but Wolves take a slim 1-0 victory.
 After failing to take any shots in the first half, the Hornets managed four in the second half to make it a nervier end for the home fans. None were on target though.
 It's Wolves' first home victory in three. Not a particularly assuring performance in front of the net for those at Molineux but it takes them to fourth.

 FULL-TIME published at 16:55 BST 16:55 BST 
 Lincoln 4-1 Burnley 
 The end of the road for Nicky Hayen at Burnley?
 Lincoln get their first home win of the season in some style.
 The flagging Clarets mired in the bottom three.

 FULL-TIME published at 16:55 BST 16:55 BST 
 West Ham 2-3 Southampton 
 Image source, Getty Images There's the whistle and Southampton win it! 
 The London Stadium errupt into boos after a Southampton defender blocks a cross out for a corner, but referee Michael Salisbury blows his whistle before they have a chance to take it. 
 West Ham made it nervy for the Saints in the end but the visitors leave the capital with the points. 
 593 134 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 FULL-TIME published at 16:55 BST 16:55 BST 
 Cardiff 1-0 Birmingham 
 A much-deserved victory for Cardiff City, who are putting together an excellent string of results.
 The Bluebirds are now unbeaten in their past three and have won three of their past five games. 
 They end Birmingham's five-game unbeaten run and three-match winning streak.
 Yousef Salech with the winner having been brought into the line-up at the last minute after Krystian Bielik was injured in the warm-up.
 Salech had a penalty saved by James Beadle in the first half, before spinning and slotting home what turned out to be the only goal of the game. Quite the afternoon for the Dane.
